chunks: And in the narration of Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام:
Regarding a man who buys a garment or goods from another man and then finds a defect in it.

He عليه السلام said: If the garment remains as it is in its original state, he returns it to its owner and takes back the price. But if he has sewn the garment, dyed it, or cut it, then he returns with compensation equal to the diminution caused by the defect.

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the purchase price paid for the item
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment being bought and examined for defect
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: goods or merchandise purchased in a transaction
key_terms.بِنُقْصَانِ الْعَيْبِ: compensation corresponding to the diminution in value due to the defect
key_terms.صَبَغَهُ: dyed it, as an example of alteration to the purchased item
key_terms.عَيْبًا: a defect found in the purchased item

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer discovers a defect in a garment after altering it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sale transactions when a defect is discovered in purchased goods. If the item remains unchanged, it may be returned for a full refund; if the buyer has altered it, he is instead entitled to the amount corresponding to the loss in value caused by the defect.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3803 - In the narration of Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them):
Regarding a man who buys a garment or merchandise from another man and then discovers a defect in it.
Imam (as) said: "If the garment is still intact as it was, he can return it to its owner and take back the price.
But if he has sewn the garment, dyed it, or cut it, then he shall return the value of the defect."
